questions.prompt: You roll one fair six-sided die once. Each face 1–6 is equally likely. What is P(rolling a 4)?
You flip one fair coin once. What is P(landing heads)?
Spin a fair spinner split into **8 equal wedges**: 6 say “Snack” and 2 say “Chore.” What is P(landing on Snack)?
Using the same 8-equal-wedge spinner (6 Snack, 2 Chore), what is P(**not** landing on Snack)?
A bag has **24** candies: **9** strawberry, **7** lemon, **8** grape. One candy is drawn at random (each candy equally likely). What is P(lemon)?
Folded slips labelled **Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun** are tossed in a hat. You draw one slip at random. What is P(Saturday)?
You flip **two** fair coins: a nickel and a dime. The ordered outcomes **HH, HT, TH, TT** are equally likely (H = heads). What is P(**exactly two** heads)?
Same two-coin experiment (four equally likely outcomes **HH, HT, TH, TT**). What is P(**exactly one** head)?
You roll **one fair die** labelled 1–6. What is P(rolling **less than** 5)?
A raffle bin contains 250 uniquely numbered tickets. Mrs. Chen bought 35 of those tickets. One ticket is drawn at random to pick the winner. What is Mrs. Chen’s probability of winning?
The school library lends 42 paperback novels in one bin: 18 mysteries, 10 fantasies, and 14 graphic novels. One book is withdrawn at random. What is P(graphic novel)?
Mr. Rao spun the same carnival wheel 200 times. It landed purple 134 times. Using those results alone, what fraction best estimates how often purple appears on that wheel in the next long run?

Tiles in a sack are labelled 10, 20, 40, or 120 (only those four slips). Each slip feels identical to the touch and one slip is pulled without peeking. What best describes pulling a slip showing the number “17”?
choices: It is impossible—the sack never contains seventeen.
It is equally likely versus every counting number.
It is guaranteed because seventeen is neat.
It depends on shouting the number seventeen beforehand.
questions.answer: It is impossible—the sack never contains seventeen.

questions.prompt: Which probability value is **not allowed** because probabilities must lie between **0** and **1** (inclusive)?
A fair coin already showed **tails** twice in a row. On the **next** flip the coin stays fair. What real probability backs **tails**?
choices: 1/2 — earlier flips carry no mechanical memory
questions.answer: 1/2 — earlier flips carry no mechanical memory
